correctness.rationale: The rank-one integral has trace norm bounded by the domain area, and its squared trace energy is the double integral of the squared normalized Bergman overlap. The weight gives kernel (1−z w̄)^−λ and dν=(1/2) du dθ, so the mean-zero graph has exactly area πU and the energy has prefactor 1/4. Differentiating upper limits gives E′ proportional to angular mean and E″=(C/2)∫f²+(1/2)∬f(θ)f(φ)B(θ−φ), with C the integrated single radial kernel derivative at U and B the two-boundary kernel. The derivatives at U are bounded also as the inner radial coordinate goes to zero. To fix C independently, the real translated circle satisfies |z−a|²=ρ²|1−az|² with ρ²=U/(1+U); differentiation gives boundary u-velocity 2√(U(U+1)) cos θ. The translation preserves both area and overlap integral, so the first variation applied to its acceleration vanishes by the area constraint and the cosine is in the Hessian kernel. With the stated Fourier normalization this gives C=−2πc₁; convolution, Parseval and the Taylor factor 1/2 yield exactly π²(c₁−c_|n|) in the deficit. The Gamma representation has a positive Bessel weight. The recurrences give (I_{n+1}/I_n)′=1−(2n+1)(I_{n+1}/I_n)/x−(I_{n+1}/I_n)²; the positive ratio starts at zero and cannot first reach one with negative derivative. Thus the coefficients are strictly decreasing and positive, and vanish at infinity by Riemann–Lebesgue. Only n=±1 are flat on the mean-zero space; equality on the nontranslation subspace is exactly the pure second harmonic. Expanding the two binomial factors at t=U/(1+U) yields the hypergeometric series; at λ=2, U=1 the geometric sums give (5+3n)/(27·2ⁿ), hence 5π²/216 for cos(2θ). The Cayley/Bergman wavelet interpretation concerns the Cauchy window with Fourier exponent (λ−1)/2 under the matching positive normalization, not another wavelet class.
residual_risks: Fixed-profile small-ε expansion only. Removing first harmonics is a Hessian restriction, not a proved uniform nonlinear stability estimate. Finite quadrature is not needed by the proof.

value.rationale: The full Hessian answers a natural stability question that disk optimality alone leaves open: it separates geometric translations from true deformations and quantifies which shape mode produces the least quadratic loss in the HS objective. The exact sharp gap for all disk areas and weights provides local conditioning for this natural localization functional, not just a sample computation or a restatement of global optimality.
residual_risks: No uniform nonlinear or operator-norm stability theorem follows from this review.
